terms.name: First Amendment Rights
terms.definition: This category covers what rights a person has under the First Amendment of the US Constitution, like to freedom of speech, freedom of religion, freedom of the press, right to assemble, and right to pettion. These rights may arise when a person think that the government is trying to interfere with their religious practices, their speaking or publishing infomration, their assembly or protests, or petitioning the government.

terms.name: First Amendment protections of freedom of religion
terms.definition: This category covers situations where a person feels their freedom of religion is being limited by a government agent, or that the government is attempting to establish a national religion. The Constitution's First Amendment prohibits laws that attempt to establish a national religion, or that impede the free exercise of a religion.

terms.name: First Amendment protections of freedom of association
terms.definition: This category covers what rights a person has under the First Amendment to associate with others, including to organize around political and social ideas that might challenge the government.

terms.name: First Amendment protections of freedom of speech
terms.definition: This category covers what rights a person has under the First Amendment freedom of speech clause, including to express themselves and protest without the government interfering in this expression.

terms.name: LGBTQ Rights
terms.definition: This category covers what protections and rights that members of the LGBTQ (lesbian, gay, bisexual, and transgender) community may have, based on their sexual orientation and gender identity. This includes protections for same-sex marriage, discrimination, and hate crimes.

terms.name: Human Rights
terms.definition: This category is about human rights protections, abuses, and claims.

terms.name: Workers' Rights
terms.definition: This category covers rights that employees and other works have when it comes to their compensation, harassment, medical or family leave, insurance, safety protections, and other rights they may have. This includes rights for special categories of work or employees, like agricultural work, immigrant workers, undocumented workers, or sex workers.

terms.name: Agricultural workers' protections
terms.definition: This category covers what rights and special protections agricultural (farm) workers have -- especially under the special federal laws like the Migrant and Seasonal Agricultural Worker Protection Act (MSPA). These include obligations that employers have around labor standards and communication, as well as what workers and contractors must do in terms of registering with the US Department of Labor.

terms.name: Mental Health Rights
terms.definition: This category covers the rights that a person experiencing mental health issues might have, particularly in situations where there are questions of decisions about medical treatment, or there are situations of discrimination, loss of liberty, or loss of autonomy.

terms.name: Rights to refuse mental health treatment
terms.definition: This category covers what rights a person has to refuse a possible treatment for mental health issues.

terms.name: Right to mental health treatment
terms.definition: This category covers what rights a person has to get treatment, and other health and medical care for their mental health issues.

terms.name: Prisoners' Rights
terms.definition: This category covers what rights a person might have while they are in a jail or prison.

terms.name: Women's Rights
terms.definition: This category covers rights and options that women have if they are facing discrimination, harassment, unequal treatment, limits on their health care or reproductive rights, access to benefits, or other issues based on their gender.

terms.name: Reproductive rights
terms.definition: Legal issues related to a person’s ability to make decisions about reproduction, including access to contraception, abortion, fertility treatment, prenatal and maternal care, and protection from coercion or discrimination in exercising these choices.

terms.name: Privacy Rights and Protections
terms.definition: This category covers what rights and protections a person has about privacy, including to information about their health, schooling, work, finances, online activity, and other decisions and behavior. This includes constitutional rights to privacy, to be protected from interference by outsiders. It includes options a person might have under different state's laws to protect their personal information or make claims against those people they think have violated their privacy.

terms.name: Address confidentiality and hiding personal location from public records
terms.definition: This category covers options a person has to keep their home address and other details hidden from public records when they are concerned about their safety. Many states have Address Confidentiality Programs (sometimes called "Safe at Home") that give survivors of domestic violence, stalking, trafficking, or sexual assault a substitute mailing address to use on public records like voter registration, court filings, driver's licenses, and school enrollment. This category covers who is eligible for these programs, how to apply, what records the substitute address covers, and how long the protection lasts. It also covers other ways a person might remove or shield their address from court records, property records, and online databases, as well as name changes done for safety reasons.

terms.name: Rights against government searches or arrests
terms.definition: This category covers what rights a person might have when dealing with a government agent who is attempting to either search their property, home, or body -- or who is attempting to arrest or detain them. This may be called 'search and seizure' or 4th Amendment issues. This includes issues of what searches and seizures are reasonable, and which are prohibited.

terms.name: Right to Travel
terms.definition: This category covers the Constitutional right to travel, including to cross state borders, without the government interfering.

terms.name: Sex workers' Rights
terms.definition: This category covers rights and protections that people in sex work may have, and how they can make use of them.

terms.name: Human Trafficking rights and protections
terms.definition: This category covers the rights of people who have been through human trafficking. This includes protection from prosecution and options for visas or immigration statuses.

terms.name: Religious Freedoms and Discrimination
terms.definition: This category covers protections and rights of people based on their belonging to an organized religious group, or based on their religious or moral beliefs. It covers issues around harassment, discrimination, interference with practicing of religion, reasonable accommodation, dressing and grooming, and other issues.

terms.name: Racial Justice and discrimination
terms.definition: This category covers rights and options for people facing discrimination, harassment, unequal treatment, and other disproportionate harm based on their race.

terms.name: Age Discrimination
terms.definition: This category covers situations where a person may have experienced discrimination based on their age. This could be at work, in a consumer context, or by other private or government actors.

terms.name: Rights when dealing with the government
terms.definition: This category covers what rights a person has when dealing with government agents like police, prosecutors, courts, administrative agencies, prison officials, and others. This includes rights and protections for when someone is under investigation, having to go to court, applying for government benefits, protesting, or other activities that might put them in contact with the government.

terms.name: Language Access rights
terms.definition: This category covers people's rights to get assistance with English in order to access government services and public programs, including rights to have an interpreter, to have important documents translated into another language, and to register complaints if they don't get equal treatment based on their language.

terms.name: Senior citizens' rights
terms.definition: Legal issues related to the rights, protections, and benefits of older adults, including age-based protections, access to services, and protection from abuse, neglect, or exploitation. This legal issue covers questions and concerns from older adults who want to understand their legal rights as seniors. It includes rights related to housing, health care, finances, employment, public benefits, decision-making, and personal autonomy, as well as protections designed to prevent abuse, neglect, or exploitation. This category also includes issues involving age discrimination, access to government or community services, and understanding how laws change or apply as people age. Seniors may seek guidance about their rights when interacting with landlords, employers, caregivers, financial institutions, or government agencies, especially when facing health changes, mobility challenges, or increasing dependence on others. In addition, this issue serves as an entry point to more specific elder law concerns, such as guardianship, powers of attorney, elder abuse, long-term care, and public benefits. Legal considerations often involve federal, state, and local protections that recognize the unique vulnerabilities and rights of older adults. Includes: General questions about legal rights of seniors Age discrimination and age-based protections Rights related to housing, health care, and benefits Financial protections and consumer rights for seniors Protection from abuse, neglect, or exploitation

terms.name: Accidents and Torts
terms.definition: This category covers problems that one person has with another person (or animal), like when there is a car accident, a dog bite, bullying or possible harassment, or neighbors treating each other badly.

terms.name: Being Physically injured or harmed by another
terms.definition: This category covers options, rights, and services for a person who has been physically hurt or killed by another person (or entity's) actions. This category covers what they might be able to do to protect themselves, get financial or medical coverage, make themselves whole, and possibly punish the other person. This might cover scenarios like being injured while getting medical care, interacting with a car, domestic violence, or otherwise.

terms.name: Suing a person or business for a personal injury
terms.definition: This category covers how a person might pursue a personal injury lawsuit against another person or a business if they have been injured. It covers who is able to sue, and what rights and processes they will have when pursuing this lawsuit.

terms.name: Personal data privacy breach and protections
terms.definition: This category covers process and options for a person who is concerned that their personal data has been accessed by another person inappropriately, that a company or controller of their data has had a breach that leaked their data, or wants to assert their privacy and data rights.

terms.name: Getting Care and Compensation for an injury
terms.definition: This category covers options that a person has to get care for when they are injured physically, emotionally, or otherwise by another person or entity. This might be around getting medical care to deal with the injuries, insurance coverage to cover the costs, or other kinds of support to help be 'made whole' again.

terms.name: Suing someone or being sued
terms.definition: This category is about the process and options for a person who either wants to sue another for a harm or injury they have experienced, or who has been sued by another person for an injury. It covers the process of how to initiate a lawsuit, how to respond to it, what rights and obligations both have, and how to deal with the final judgment.

terms.name: Car Accident lawsuits
terms.definition: This category concerns the process of suing someone, or being sued, for injuries around a car accident. It could be injuries to a person's body or to the property. This covers the steps to take in the lawsuit, what kinds of claims are possible, and what resolutions and consequences there might be.

terms.name: Being a Plaintiff in lawsuit (suing someone)
terms.definition: This category covers the options, process, and obligations of a person who is suing another person or entity, for a harm from an injury that has happened.

terms.name: Being a Defendant in a lawsuit (being sued)
terms.definition: This category covers the options, rights, and obligations of a person who is being sued in court for an injury (or tort) that another person alleges has happened. This includes how the court process will work, how a person can defend themselves, and what consequences they might face.

terms.name: Seeking an injunction to compel an action
terms.definition: This category covers how a person might sue another party for 'injunctive relief', in which they want that party to do certain acts or behave in a certain way. This is one remedy that could be claimed along with money damages.

terms.name: Suing to enforce a law (Private right of action)
terms.definition: This category covers situations when a person might want to enforce a law or legal requirement. They may try to use a private right of action to bring a lawsuit to enforce the law.

terms.name: Outcomes a plaintiff can seek in a lawsuit
terms.definition: This category covers what a person can try to get a court order for, in a civil lawsuit against another party. This may be called remedies. It could include money damages, injunctions, or other things for the court to order.

terms.name: Suing the government for civil rights violations
terms.definition: This category covers a person's options to sue the government for possible civil rights violations they have suffered by a government agency or official. This might be called a Section 1983 lawsuit. It might involve lawsuits against the police for the use of excessive force.

terms.name: Suing the government for a tort (Tort Claims Act)
terms.definition: A lawsuit against a government entity under a federal or state tort claims act.

terms.name: Harassment by another person
terms.definition: This category covers the options and rights of a person who is facing harassment by another person (including threatening behavior, stalking, harassing behavior online or in texting, sexual harassment at work or otherwise, or other inappropriate behavior). This category also covers options and protections if a person is being accused of harassing another person, and what process and consequences they might face, as well as how they might defend themselves. This includes harassment that might be considered under civil laws, or that might cross over to criminal laws. It also covers the difference between domestic violence and harassment (by non-family members, or more distant family members).

terms.name: Suing someone for defamation
terms.definition: Legal issues related to filing a lawsuit for defamation based on false statements that harm a person’s or business’s reputation, including claims involving libel (written statements) or slander (spoken statements). It may involve questions about proof of falsity, harm, defenses such as truth or opinion, and special rules for public figures or online speech.

terms.name: Nuisance or harassment by a neighbor
terms.definition: Legal issues related to ongoing nuisance or harassing behavior by a neighbor that interferes with a person’s ability to safely and peacefully use their home or property. This includes conduct that is threatening, intimidating, disruptive, or persistently disturbing. This issue covers situations where a neighbor engages in repeated or severe behavior such as excessive noise, verbal abuse, threats, stalking, intimidation, property interference, or other actions that substantially interfere with quiet enjoyment or personal safety. It may involve disputes between homeowners, renters, or mixed settings, and can occur in single-family neighborhoods, apartment buildings, or shared communities. It also includes understanding what legal protections and remedies may be available, such as documenting incidents, requesting landlord or HOA intervention, seeking restraining or protective orders, filing complaints with local authorities, or pursuing civil remedies. Legal questions may involve local nuisance laws, harassment standards, evidentiary requirements, and how to address retaliation or escalation. Rules and options vary by jurisdiction and the nature of the conduct. Includes: - Ongoing noise or disruptive behavior by a neighbor - Threats, intimidation, or harassment - Stalking or repeated unwanted contact - Interference with quiet enjoyment of property - Landlord or HOA responsibilities to address neighbor conduct - Legal options to stop or prevent continued harassment

terms.name: Online harassment- cyberbullying and doxing
terms.definition: Civil legal issues from online harassment, cyberbullying, doxing, or threats through digital platforms.

terms.name: Traffic and Cars
terms.definition: This category covers problems with traffic and parking tickets, fees, driver's licenses, and other issues experienced with the traffic system. It also concerns issues with car accidents and injuries, cars' quality, repairs, purchases, and other contracts.

terms.name: Car injuries to people or property
terms.definition: This category is about what options or rights a person has if they have been injured by a car, or if they might have injured another person or property with their car. It could be based on the manufacturer's car vehicle defect or recall, or it could be around another person's driving. It covers what options this person might have, including filing a lawsuit to recover damages for the injury.

terms.name: Dealing with traffic and parking tickets
terms.definition: This category covers issues a person might have when driving a car, including problems with driving, driving under the influence, or problems with one's license or insurance. This covers responding to tickets and going to court.

terms.name: Speeding and Moving Violations
terms.definition: This category covers a person's options if they are facing a ticket for speeding, running a red light, or other problem with their driving.

terms.name: License and Registration Traffic Tickets
terms.definition: This category covers issues a person might have when they have gotten a ticket for issues with their driver's license or registration.

terms.name: No Insurance Traffic Tickets
terms.definition: This category covers issues a person might have if they have a ticket for driving without insurance, or driving without proof of insurance.

terms.name: Parking Tickets
terms.definition: This category covers issues a person might have for a parking ticket, around how their car was parked.

terms.name: Driving Under the Influence
terms.definition: This category covers options and rights for a person who is charged with driving under the influence (DUI), and what consequences they may face.

terms.name: Going to Traffic Court
terms.definition: This category covers how a person can go to traffic court to respond to a ticket, contest it, or see what options are available to resolve it.

terms.name: Driver's licenses or permits
terms.definition: This category concerns how an individual gets and maintains a driver's license or permit, to operate a car, motorcycle, truck, or other motor vehicle.

terms.name: Driver's License Suspension
terms.definition: This category covers how a person might have their driver's license suspended or taken away, how to contest this, and how to deal with the suspension. This could cover suspensions for traffic tickets, or for deteriorating health or ability to drive.

terms.name: Reinstating a Driver's License
terms.definition: This category covers how a person can have their driver's license reinstated after

terms.name: Commercial driver's license (CDL) issues
terms.definition: Legal issues specific to CDL violations, suspensions, and disqualifications.

terms.name: Issues with Owning a Car
terms.definition: This category concerns issues with owning a car, including how to pay for it, getting insurance for it, repairing it, warranties on it, and dealing with possible repossession.

terms.name: Car Payment Issues
terms.definition: This category concerns problems a person might have with meeting payments for their car or car insurance -- and what options they might have.

terms.name: Issues with Purchasing and Financing a Car
terms.definition: This category concerns issues with purchasing a car, including getting financing, reviewing the contract, understanding the loan terms, and having your credit report assessed.

terms.name: Car Repair issues
terms.definition: This category concerns issues with having a car repaired, paying for it, refusing to pay, dealing with a mechanic's lien, and protection against unfair or deceptive trade practices for car repair estimates and use of rebuilt parts in the repairs.

terms.name: Warranties and contracts for a car
terms.definition: This category concerns problems around 'vehicle warranties' for a car that one has purchased, which a person might have purchased to protect against unexpected or costly repairs or that might come with a manufacturer's warranty. It covers auto service contracts, warranty coverage, disputes around these warranties, how to make a claim, and state/federal lemon laws that relate to vehicle warranties.

terms.name: Vehicle/Auto License or Registration
terms.definition: This category concerns the process and options of getting a license or other official registration for a vehicle, like a car, so that it can be legally permitted to be used.

terms.name: Vehicle towing disputes
terms.definition: Disputes with towing companies including challenging a tow and disputing fees.

terms.name: Car insurance
terms.definition: This category concerns issues with having insurance for a car one is using, including purchasing it, making claims, getting temporary insurance for a rental, and dealing with the insurance company.

terms.name: Being in a car accident without insurance
terms.definition: Legal issues related to being involved in a motor vehicle accident while uninsured, including liability, fines or penalties, limits on recovery, and dealing with claims, lawsuits, or license consequences. It often involves state-specific rules affecting fault, damages, and whether an uninsured driver can recover compensation.

terms.name: Being arrested for traffic violation
terms.definition: Legal issues related to being arrested for a traffic-related offense classified as a gross misdemeanor, including understanding charges, arrest procedures, court process, and potential penalties. This issue covers situations where a traffic violation results in arrest rather than a citation, such as serious driving offenses, repeat violations, or conduct that elevates the charge to a gross misdemeanor. It includes understanding why an arrest occurred, what the charge means, and what steps follow arrest, including booking, bail or release conditions, and upcoming court appearances. It also includes navigating the criminal court process for gross misdemeanor traffic offenses, such as arraignment, pretrial hearings, and possible outcomes. Legal questions may involve defenses, license consequences, fines, jail exposure, probation terms, and the impact of a conviction on driving privileges, employment, or insurance. Procedures and penalties vary by jurisdiction and offense. Includes: - Arrests for traffic offenses classified as gross misdemeanors - Booking, bail, and release procedures - Court process and hearings for traffic-related criminal charges - Potential penalties, including fines, jail, and probation - Driver’s license suspension or revocation related to the arrest - Collateral consequences affecting employment or insurance

terms.name: Work and Employment Law
terms.definition: This category covers issues related to working at a job, including discrimination and harassment, worker's compensation, workers rights, unions, getting paid, pensions, being fired, and more. Scenarios in this category include an employer who did not pay wages or other earned benefits, denial of worker’s compensation, unsafe working conditions, unfair termination, denial of accommodation for disability or a medical condition, denial of unemployment benefits, inadequate treatment of a workplace grievance, and sexual harassment by a supervisor or coworker.

terms.name: Applying and interviewing for a job
terms.definition: This category covers issues that might arise while a person is trying to get a job, including rights and discrimination, background checks, criminal records, drug testing, affirmative action, and inappropriate behavior.

terms.name: Being drug tested when applying for a job
terms.definition: This category covers a job applicant's rights and options if a potential employer is asking them to take a drug or alcohol test as part of the application process. This includes options to refuse a drug test, what rights you have if you fail the drug test, and what rules the employer must follow to correctly do drug testing without discrimination or inaccuracies.

terms.name: Affirmative Action for employment
terms.definition: This category covers if and whether affirmative action policies will affect a person who is applying for a job. It covers the rules that might determine if an employer can or should promote job opportunities for specific groups of people, like people of color, women, people with disabilities, or military veterans.

terms.name: Criminal record and background check issues while applying for jobs
terms.definition: This category covers issues a person may face when an employer runs a background check or asks about criminal history during the hiring process. This includes what an employer is allowed to ask about arrests and convictions, what shows up on a background check, how to dispute inaccurate information on a background report, and what protections exist under "ban the box" or fair chance hiring laws. It also covers a person's rights if they are denied a job because of their criminal record, including whether the employer followed required procedures like providing a copy of the report and a chance to respond. The category connects to expungement and record sealing for people who want to clean their record before applying.

terms.name: Problems at a Current Job
terms.definition: This category is about problems that might arise while working at a job, including around proper payment and benefits, discrimination, inappropriate behavior, health issues and disabilities, immigration, training, and more.

terms.name: Privacy at work
terms.definition: Legal issues related to an employee’s right to privacy in the workplace. This includes concerns about employer monitoring, searches, access to personal information, medical confidentiality, and surveillance. This issue covers situations where an employee believes their employer has improperly monitored communications, searched personal belongings, accessed private accounts, disclosed medical information, or installed surveillance without proper notice. Questions often arise about privacy in emails, text messages, social media, personal devices used for work, locker or desk searches, drug testing, background checks, and workplace cameras. It also includes understanding the limits of workplace privacy protections, which may depend on employer policies, whether equipment is employer-owned, consent forms, union agreements, and federal or state laws. Legal questions may involve data protection rules, confidentiality of personnel files, medical privacy laws, and protections against intrusive or discriminatory practices. Privacy rights at work vary significantly by jurisdiction and by the nature of the workplace. Includes: - Employer monitoring of emails, devices, or internet use - Workplace searches of desks, lockers, or personal items - Surveillance cameras and audio recording concerns - Disclosure of medical or personal information - Background checks and drug testing - Limits and protections for employee privacy

terms.name: Being tested for drugs or alcohol at work
terms.definition: This category covers an employee's rights and options if an employer is asking them to take a drug or alcohol test as part of their job. This includes options to refuse a drug test, what rights you have if you fail the drug test, and what rules the employer must follow to correctly do drug testing without discrimination or inaccuracies. It also includes an employee's ability to challenge a drug test, and when employers are allowed to require a test based on 'reasonable suspicion'.

terms.name: Wage payment - hours and breaks at work
terms.definition: This category covers issues an employee may have with how much they are getting paid, if they are getting adequate overtime, if employers are requiring workers to clock out during breaks, if the employer is paying less than the minimum wage, or if there are other claims/problems around the amount paid for the hours worked. This might include topics like 'wage theft', when workers are not being paid what is owed to them.

terms.name: Minors' protections and restrictions at work
terms.definition: This category covers the legal limits on the employment of minors (people under the age of 18). This includes whether the minors can be employed at all, what jobs are considered too hazardous to have minors employed, what limits on hours or activities there might be, and what extra protections they might have at work.

terms.name: Being an Employee vs. an Independent Contractor
terms.definition: This category covers questions a worker might have about their relationship with the organization they're working for, including if you have been misclassified as an independent contractor rather than an employee.

terms.name: Being a subcontractor
terms.definition: This category covers the rights, obligations, and duties of subcontractor workers, who work for 'general contractors' at a job. This includes what obligations the employer and the general contractor have toward them, what tax and contract obligations subcontractors have, and what protections they have regarding wages, breaks, working conditions, termination, and other situations.

terms.name: Taking Time off Work at Current Job
terms.definition: About taking time off from a current job because of illness, adoption, bereavement, religious reasons, military service, disability treatment, domestic violence, or other reasons

terms.name: Reasonable accommodation for a disability at work
terms.definition: This category covers how a person might request a reasonable accommodation for a disability at their job, what their rights are, what employers are required to do, and how to deal with issues with the request.

terms.name: Problems regarding a Former Job
terms.definition: This category is about the period after leaving a job, including being fired or quitting, severance agreements, non-compete contracts, references, personnel files, getting back pay, and harassment.

terms.name: Being fired after whistleblowing
terms.definition: This category covers options and rights for a person who has been terminated from their job after being a whistleblower regarding illegal activity by their employer. This includes when whistleblowers have protections against termination, retaliation, or ability to make claims to be compensated for being fired.

terms.name: Being fired from a job
terms.definition: This category covers issues a person might have after they have been terminated from their job. It includes the possibility to raise a 'wrongful termination' claim, when employers are allowed to let a worker go, what reasons are acceptable for it, and what a worker can do if they think they have been fired illegally or in a way that is against public policy (like for retaliation or discrimination).

terms.name: Employment records from former job
terms.definition: This category covers how a person might request their personnel file from a former employer, how other possible employers might request your past employment records, and deal with other issues about what a previous employer says or releases about your work history.

terms.name: Severance packages and negotiation
terms.definition: Legal review and negotiation of severance packages including non-competes and releases. This relates to when a person is let go from a job, and is negotiating their exit package.

terms.name: Retirement and Pensions
terms.definition: This category is about getting payments and benefits after retiring from a job or at the end of a career. This includes around eligibility for benefits, proper management of benefit plans under ERISA, vesting of benefits, managers of benefits, and railroad retirement.

terms.name: Mismanagement of retirement and pension plans (under ERISA)
terms.definition: This category covers what employees can do if they believe that their employer has violated their obligations to properly manage retirement, pension, and profit-sharing plans under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act (ERISA). This includes obligations to provide benefits to current or former employees, to maintain their fiduciary duties toward the employees, and to protect their rights.

terms.name: Retirement and pension plan disputes
terms.definition: Disputes about retirement and pension benefits including PERS and similar state programs.

terms.name: Eligibility for pension plan or retirement benefits
terms.definition: This category covers questions around whether a person is eligible to join a pension plan or get retirement benefits through their work.

terms.name: Vesting of retirement plan
terms.definition: This category covers issues around when an employee's retirement plans vest, meaning that they have ownership over the account balance that the employer cannot take away. This includes rules around losing retirement benefits if a person leaves the job or works less than a certain number of hours. It also includes rules around when there must e 100% vesting.

terms.name: Railroad workers' retirement system
terms.definition: This category covers issues around railroad retirement benefits. This is typically eligible to railroad workers and their families through the federal agency Railroad Retirement Board. This category covers eligibility, overpayments, benefit appeals, and other resources.

terms.name: Unions
terms.definition: This category is about forming unions, joining them, rights as a union member, dealing with possible problems, and opting out of a union.

terms.name: Employer interfering with union activity (Unfair Labor Practices)
terms.definition: This category covers protections and issues for employees who are facing interference by their employer, when trying to organize, join, or assist a union. It also covers what kinds of employee activities are protected as concerted activities, like conversations, posting on social media, or collective bargaining. This is in part defined by the National Labor Relations Act, and other labor laws, that lay out protections for employees and unions.

terms.name: Unfair Labor Practices by Unions
terms.definition: This category covers restrictions on what unions can do at a workplace, under laws around unfair labor practices. This includes situations when unions may be restraining or coercing employees regarding their choice not to support a union, crossing a picket line, restraining an employer's choice of bargaining representative, causing employers to penalize employees who engage in anti-union activities, or charging excessive fees. This category covers how an employee might make a complaint to the NLRB about these practices, and what rights they have.

terms.name: Workers' rights to discuss pay and organize together
terms.definition: This category covers the rights employees have to talk with each other about wages, hours, and working conditions, and to act together to improve their workplace. Under federal labor law (the National Labor Relations Act), most private-sector employees are protected when they discuss pay with coworkers, share information about working conditions on social media or messaging platforms like Slack, sign petitions, or coordinate to raise concerns with management as a group. These protections apply whether or not a union exists or is being formed. This category covers what counts as "protected concerted activity," what employers are not allowed to do in response (like firing, disciplining, or threatening workers for these conversations), what workplace policies around pay secrecy or social media may be unlawful, and how to file a complaint with the National Labor Relations Board if an employer retaliates. It also covers which workers are not covered by the NLRA, like independent contractors, supervisors, agricultural workers, and public-sector employees who may have separate state-level protections.

terms.name: Volunteering or interning at a job
terms.definition: About rights and duties of people who are interning or volunteering at a job.

terms.name: Being injured on the job
terms.definition: This category is about options that a person has after there has been health or physical injuries that happen while on the job. It includes how to report it, how to get workers compensation coverage for it, and what other protections and options the employee has. It also includes if an existing medical condition is made worse by workplace conditions. This category also covers if a person is able to sue their employer for their injury, or what they might do if the employer retaliates or discriminates against them after the injury.

terms.name: Getting Worker's Compensation benefits
terms.definition: This category covers if and how an employee can get Worker's Compensation benefits. The laws vary state to state, but generally workers who are injured on the job or have a sickness or disability that is made worse by workplace conditions can access workers' compensation to help them cover their costs. This also covers whether Worker's Compensation programs stop an employee from being able to sue their employer for their injury.

terms.name: Working conditions that are unsafe or unhealthy
terms.definition: This category covers an employee's options if they are working in a place that seems to have health or safety hazards. This could be for dangerous machines, toxic chemicals, or poor training. This category includes the ability to file complaints with the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), to get the workplace inspected and improved. It also covers what happens if an employee faces retaliation for making a complaint.

terms.name: Employer obligations for workers' compensation
terms.definition: Employer's legal obligations around workers' comp coverage, reporting, and non-retaliation.

terms.name: Third-party claims related to a workplace injury
terms.definition: Lawsuits against third parties whose negligence contributed to a workplace injury.

terms.name: Discrimination around work and employment
terms.definition: This category is about possible discrimination around employment, based on disability, ethnicity, gender, marital status, race, religion, sexual harassment, sexual orientation, or age. It also includes what remedies an employee might be eligible to receive, if they have been discriminated against.

terms.name: Remedies for discrimination at work
terms.definition: This category covers what an employee (or potential employee) might be eligible to receive if they have faced discrimination in their employment. This includes options to get back pay, compensatory damages, or punitive damages for the discrimination they have faced.

terms.name: Sexual harassment at work
terms.definition: This category covers situations when a person is facing sexual harassment at work or an interview for employment, including propositions, jokes, touching, and other physical or verbal conduct that is sexual in nature. This category includes the standards of what constitutes sexual harassment, how to make complaints, what workers' or applicants' rights are, and steps they can take to protect themselves.

terms.name: Age discrimination at work
terms.definition: This category covers options and rights for a person who may be facing inappropriate treatment at work (or potential work) based on their age. This includes around their hiring, firing, pay, job assignments, promotions, or comments and insults. The category covers what the standards for discrimination are, and what a person can do to protect themselves.

terms.name: Disability discrimination at work
terms.definition: This category covers options and rights for a person who may be facing inappropriate treatment at work (or potential work) based on their disability. This includes around their hiring, firing, pay, job assignments, promotions, or comments and insults. The category covers what the standards for discrimination are, and what a person can do to protect themselves.

terms.name: Gender discrimination at work
terms.definition: This category covers options and rights for a person who may be facing inappropriate treatment at work (or potential work) based on their gender. This includes around their hiring, firing, pay, job assignments, promotions, or comments and insults. The category covers what the standards for discrimination are, and what a person can do to protect themselves.

terms.name: Racial and Ethnic discrimination at work
terms.definition: This category covers options and rights for a person who may be facing inappropriate treatment at work (or potential work) based on their race, ethnicity, or country of origin. This includes around their hiring, firing, pay, job assignments, promotions, or comments and insults. The category covers what the standards for discrimination are, and what a person can do to protect themselves.

terms.name: Religious discrimination at work
terms.definition: This category covers options and rights for a person who may be facing inappropriate treatment at work (or potential work) based on their religion. This includes around their hiring, firing, pay, job assignments, promotions, or comments and insults. The category covers what the standards for discrimination are, and what a person can do to protect themselves.

terms.name: Sexual orientation or Gender Identity discrimination at work
terms.definition: This category covers options and rights for a person who may be facing inappropriate treatment at work (or potential work) based on their sexual orientation (real or perceived) or their gender identity. This includes around their hiring, firing, pay, job assignments, promotions, or comments and insults. The category covers what the standards for discrimination are, and what a person can do to protect themselves.

terms.name: Martial or Parental Status discrimination at work
terms.definition: This category covers options and rights for a person who may be facing inappropriate treatment at work (or potential work) based on their family status -- like around having children, being married, single, divorced, widowed, or head of household. This includes around their hiring, firing, pay, job assignments, promotions, or comments and insults. The category covers what the standards for discrimination are, and what a person can do to protect themselves.

terms.name: Proving discrimination at work
terms.definition: This category covers the legal standards and types of behavior that apply when a worker is bringing a complaint of discrimination against an employer.

terms.name: Employment in prison
terms.definition: This category is about opportunities to work while in a prison. It also concerns rights, payments, and other concerns of people who are employed while in prison. This could be about work programs and work release programs.

terms.name: Veterans and Military members' Civilian Work
terms.definition: This category is about rights and remedies when a person returns to civilian work after serving in the military, including dealing with problems with pay, promotions, and seniority that can be addressed through USSERA.

terms.name: Uniform Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act for servicemembers
terms.definition: This category covers military servicemembers' and veterans' rights under the Uniform Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act (USERRA). This includes obligations for employers to put servicemembers back in their civilian jobs after military service. It also is about how they can seek employment without discrimination based on their military service.

terms.name: Suing an employer for a tort
terms.definition: This category covers options for a person to sue an employer while working there or after leaving their job. It might be for tort claims for negligence around a safe workplace, fraud (when an employer deceives them), defamation (when an employer lies about them), false imprisonment (for not allowing them to leave), or for assault and battery (for allowing them to be injured on the job).

terms.name: Public employee and civil service protections
terms.definition: Legal issues for government employees including civil service protections and public sector labor rights.
